privacy.title: Privacy — Papel Tools
privacy.h1: Your files never leave your device.
privacy.intro: Papel Tools is built around a single promise: when you convert a PDF to Markdown on this site, the file is processed entirely inside your browser. No copy of your document is sent to any server, stored in any database, or shared with any third party. This page explains exactly how we keep that promise — and how you can verify it yourself.
privacy.section1Body: We don't upload your PDF. We don't analyze its contents. We don't log filenames, page counts, or text fragments. We don't set tracking cookies on the converter page. Conversion runs inside a Web Worker in your browser tab using PDF.js and our local Markdown assembly pipeline — the bytes of your file never travel over the network.
privacy.section2Body: Open DevTools (F12 or Cmd+Opt+I) → Network tab. Clear the log, then convert a PDF. You will see no request containing your PDF bytes or extracted text. Text-based conversion normally needs no additional resources after the page loads. The first OCR run may download same-origin OCR models and WebAssembly files; those are software resources, not your document, and your PDF is never uploaded.
privacy.section3Body: We do not currently load an analytics service on this site, and the converter does not send document telemetry. Standard hosting infrastructure may retain basic request logs for page and asset delivery, but those requests do not contain your PDF, extracted text, or conversion result. If we add privacy-friendly analytics later, we will update this page before enabling it.
privacy.section4Body: We store your language preference (EN/ES/PT) in a browser cookie so the site remembers your choice. We never store your files, conversion results, or any document content. Local browser storage (IndexedDB) is used only if you opt into the conversion history feature (planned for a future release).
privacy.section5Body: We do not embed third-party trackers, advertising, or social widgets on the converter page. Fonts are self-hosted with next/font and served from the same site. On the first OCR run, the browser may download same-origin OCR models and WebAssembly resources. Blocking third-party requests does not prevent conversion because no third-party service receives your document.
privacy.section6Body: The web converter is built on open-source PDF.js and @pdf2md/core. The Papel Tools application repository is not public yet; when it is released, we will link it from this site. Until then, this privacy page and the developer documentation describe the current processing boundaries without claiming that the full application can already be audited publicly.
privacy.section7Body: Questions about privacy? Use the contact page or email us directly at the address shown there. We respond to privacy inquiries within 5 business days.

terms.title: Terms — Papel Tools
terms.h1: The simple rules of using Papel Tools.
terms.intro: These terms describe how you can use Papel Tools — a free, browser-based PDF to Markdown converter — and what we promise in return. We have tried to keep this page short and readable. If anything is unclear, contact us and we will help.
terms.section1Body: By visiting this website or using any of our tools you agree to these terms. If you do not agree, please do not use the service. The terms cover both the browser converter on this site and the remote MCP endpoint used by AI agents — the privacy and file-handling differences between the two are described in section 4.
terms.section2Body: Papel Tools converts PDF files to Markdown. The web converter runs entirely in your browser — no signup, no account, no server-side processing. The MCP endpoint is a separate hosted service that accepts PDF files uploaded by AI agents and returns Markdown; it is rate-limited and follows the limits described in our developer documentation.
terms.section3Body: You may use Papel Tools for personal, educational, or internal business work. You may not: scrape the converter to redistribute or resell its output as a competing service; run automated batch conversions that exceed the published rate limits; upload files that contain malware, illegal content, or material you do not have the right to process; or attempt to disrupt the service for other users.
terms.section4Body: The web converter does not receive your files. Conversion happens inside your browser tab using JavaScript and WebAssembly — your PDFs never leave your device, and we have no copy of them. The MCP endpoint is different: an AI agent uploads the PDF to our server once, we run the conversion, and we return the Markdown. We do not store, log, or forward the file to any third party, and we discard it as soon as the response is sent. In both cases the Markdown output belongs to you. Web fonts are self-hosted with next/font; the remote MCP endpoint uses Upstash for rate-limit data and Vercel for hosting.
terms.section5Body: Papel Tools uses open-source dependencies including PDF.js and @pdf2md/core under their respective licenses. The Papel Tools application repository is not public yet and is being prepared for a future source release. The Papel Tools name, logo, and page design may not be reused to suggest endorsement. The Markdown output you generate with the tool is yours, with no claim from us.
terms.section6Body: Papel Tools is provided "as is", without any warranty of any kind. We do not promise that conversion or OCR will be 100% accurate for every PDF, that the service will be available at any specific uptime, or that it will meet your particular requirements. The web converter offers optional on-device OCR for scanned PDFs; the hosted remote MCP endpoint does not support OCR.
terms.section7Body: To the maximum extent permitted by law, our total liability to you for any claim arising from your use of Papel Tools is capped at the greater of USD 100 or the fees you paid us in the twelve months before the claim. Because the service is free today, this effectively limits our liability to USD 100. We are not liable for indirect, incidental, or consequential damages such as lost profits, lost data, or business interruption.
terms.section8Body: We may update these terms from time to time. The change will be reflected by updating the "Last updated" date at the top of this page — please check back occasionally. If you have any questions, use the Contact link in the site footer or email us directly at the address shown on that page.

mcp.title: MCP Server Documentation — Papel Tools
mcp.intro: Expose the PDF to Markdown engine as a Model Context Protocol server — the mcp pdf converter that pairs with Claude Desktop, Cursor, and VS Code. JSON-RPC 2.0 over Streamable HTTP, OAuth-less, stateless. Add the server once and your agent can run claude mcp pdf to markdown or cursor mcp pdf workflows in the chat.
mcp.configIntro: Add the server to your MCP client. Below are copy-paste configs for the three most common clients.
mcp.claudeDesktopRestart: Save to claude_desktop_config.json and restart Claude Desktop. Your agent now exposes convert_pdf, preview_pdf, and list_supported_formats in its tool palette.
mcp.cursorNote: Cursor reads .cursor/mcp.json or its global config. Save and reload the MCP registry.
mcp.vscodeNote: Save to your extension's MCP config (Continue: ~/.continue/config.json; Cline: VS Code settings.json).
mcp.toolsIntro: The server exposes three tools. All accept Base64-encoded PDF and return Markdown + structured metadata.
mcp.convertPdfSummary: Convert a PDF file (Base64-encoded) to Markdown.
mcp.previewPdfSummary: Convert a PDF to a Markdown preview (first 4000 characters). Use this to gauge quality before committing to a full convert_pdf.
mcp.listPdfSummary: Return the remote endpoint's capability matrix. Call this before convert_pdf to validate input.
mcp.limitsIntro: The hosted MCP endpoint enforces the following limits. Use list_supported_formats at runtime to verify the current values.
limitsTable: PDF only (text-based; scanned PDFs are rejected)
mcp.privacyBody: Yes, your PDF uploads once to our server for conversion. Files are never forwarded to any third party, never stored, never logged, never used for training. The website converter (zero-upload, 100% in-browser) and the local npm stdio package (Phase 2, 100% on your machine) are alternative surfaces — choose based on your threat model.
mcp.responseIntro: All tool responses follow the MCP CallToolResult spec. Success returns structured content; failures return isError: true with structured content describing the cause.
mcp.sourceBody: The repository is not yet public — we are preparing it for an open-source release under the MIT license.
mcp.localDevBody: Local development instructions will be available when the repository is made public.
mcp.localDevCmd: # Coming soon — repository not yet public
mcp.faqSubtitle: Quick answers for developers integrating the MCP server
mcp.faq1A: No authentication in the MVP. The server is anonymous and identified by IP. Production deployments enforce an Origin whitelist via the ALLOWED_ORIGINS env var. API keys and OAuth are planned for the local stdio package in Phase 2.
mcp.faq2Q: Why is the rate limit per IP, not per API key?
mcp.faq2A: Because there are no API keys yet. Each request is anonymous and identified by the x-forwarded-for header (Vercel auto-injects this). When API keys land (Phase 2), the limit will switch to per-key.
mcp.faq3A: Yes. The structuredContent field is deterministic for a given file. Cache by hash of the Base64 input or by filename + size. The server does not set Cache-Control headers today, so client-side caching is your responsibility.
mcp.faq4Q: What error codes should I handle?
mcp.faq4A: From the ConversionError taxonomy: file_empty, file_too_big, encrypted_pdf, scanned_pdf, corrupted_pdf. Each error returns isError: true with structuredContent.error.code so your agent can branch on the failure type.

ocr.stepsTitle: How to convert a scanned PDF
ocr.stepsSubtitle: Three steps from scan to reviewable Markdown
ocr.step1Body: Choose one PDF up to 200 MB. If it has no selectable text layer, the converter detects it and offers OCR instead of returning broken Markdown.
ocr.step2Body: Select English, Spanish, or Portuguese. The first run downloads same-origin OCR model and WebAssembly resources; the PDF itself is never uploaded.
ocr.step3Body: Check names, numbers, tables, and line breaks because OCR accuracy varies with scan quality. Then copy the Markdown or download the .md file.
ocr.faq1Q: Can it convert scanned PDFs now?
ocr.faq1A: Yes. If a PDF has no selectable text layer, the converter offers on-device OCR for English, Spanish, or Portuguese. OCR runs through software loaded in your browser, and your PDF bytes and extracted text are never uploaded to Papel Tools or a third party.
ocr.faq2Q: What happens on the first OCR run?
ocr.faq2A: The browser downloads same-origin OCR model and WebAssembly resources before recognition starts. This can take longer than later runs, and the resources may be cached locally for reuse. DevTools will show these software downloads, but it will not show a request containing your PDF or extracted text.
ocr.faq3Q: How accurate is the OCR result?
ocr.faq3A: Accuracy depends on resolution, contrast, rotation, language, and page layout. Clean scans work best; handwriting, complex tables, and damaged pages may need manual correction. Review sensitive or high-stakes Markdown before using it in an LLM, knowledge base, or business workflow.
ocr.faq4Q: Does OCR run in my browser or on a server?
ocr.faq4A: The website OCR runs on your device using Tesseract.js and same-origin language resources. The hosted remote MCP endpoint is a separate product surface and does not support OCR; scanned PDFs sent to that endpoint return a clear JSON-RPC error.

tables.intro: Tables become clean GitHub-flavored Markdown — the format LLMs and RAG pipelines read best. Use it for pdf table extraction and convert pdf tables to markdown without losing structure: column alignment, merged cells, and headings all stay readable.

tables.stepsSubtitle: Three steps from PDF to Markdown with tables
tables.step1Body: Drag a PDF with tables — financial reports, research papers, product specs, datasheets. Up to 200 MB, no signup.
tables.step2Body: Each table becomes a Markdown table with | separators. Column alignment is preserved where the PDF embeds hints. Merged cells stay merged with the best-effort strategy for plain Markdown.
tables.step3Body: Paste into your LLM chat, your RAG pipeline, your docs site — GFM tables render correctly in GitHub, Obsidian, Notion, and most static site generators. No cleanup needed.
tables.faq1A: Yes. Tables become GitHub-flavored Markdown (GFM) — the | separator format that renders correctly in GitHub, Obsidian, Notion, and most static site generators. Column alignment hints from the PDF are preserved where present. If a table is too damaged to parse reliably, we flag it instead of silently producing broken Markdown.
tables.faq2Q: What about complex tables with merged cells?
tables.faq2A: We use a best-effort strategy. Merged cells are preserved by repeating the value in adjacent Markdown cells, which is the standard approach for representing merged cells in plain Markdown. It's not perfect (Markdown has no native merge syntax), but it's the best you can do without HTML — and it renders predictably in every viewer.
tables.faq3A: Nested tables are flattened with indentation hints where possible, since Markdown has no native nesting syntax for tables. For deeply nested tables, consider exporting to HTML first if your downstream tool supports it.
tables.faq4Q: Can I export tables to CSV or Excel directly?
tables.faq4A: Not yet — the converter outputs Markdown only. For CSV export, copy the Markdown table and use an online converter or `pandoc` on the command line. CSV / Excel export is on the roadmap but not in the current MVP.
